subject: 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493
fact: The events described occurred on the 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493, marking the temporal anchor for the death of the stone giant, the Duergar’s shrinking, Thorin’s encounter with Dorhun, and the expiration of Gartokkar’s offer.
source_quote: 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493

subject: 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493
fact: The events occur on the 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493, a time of escalating tension in Gracklstugh as the Deepking’s madness destabilizes the regime and factions vie for power.
source_quote: [Continuing — Date: 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493, Speaker: Daz]

subject: 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493
fact: The events occur on the 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493, marking the temporal anchor for the unfolding intrigue in Grygum and Gracklstugh.
source_quote: 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493.
source_quote: 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493

subject: appearance of second stone giant
fact: A second stone giant, flanked by Duergar and armed with stone weapons, appears immediately after Thorin’s inquiry, suggesting coordinated surveillance or intervention by the city’s powers.
source_quote: Before Thorin can ask a follow-up question, another Stone Giant appears, flanked by Duergar, armed with curious stone weapons.

subject: corruption escalation
fact: Corruption began with rule-breaking in the bazaar, escalated to grift, then chaos, and now threatens destruction, as described by Errde and confirmed by Daz’s observations.
source_quote: Things were not proceeding according to the rules of the market, of the bazaar. It starts with not obeying the rules. Then it proceeds to grift, then chaos, and then destruction.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz mutters, 'In this authoritarian, strict-as-rules city, what we saw is corruption.'
source_quote: Daz mutters, 'In this authoritarian, strict-as-rules city, what we saw is corruption.'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz wonders if they should interview the various factions to find out which one they should join or whether they should join any of them.
source_quote: Daz wonders if they should interview the various factions to find out which one they should join or whether they should join any of them.

subject: death of the two-headed stone giant
fact: The two-headed stone giant was subdued by Thorin’s attempts and Daz’s weakening spells, struck by Zalthir and Grygum, and ultimately killed by a Duergar flame device. The event triggered Thorin’s mourning, Grygum’s intervention, and the Duergar’s subsequent shrinking to standard size, indicating the completion of their ritual or magical transformation.
source_quote: The Duergar, unconvinced by Thorin’s entreaties, kill the giant.

subject: Droki’s disappearance
fact: Droki, a rogue Duergar residing in the West Cleft District among the Derro, has evaded capture. His whereabouts and motives are unknown, but his presence threatens to provoke war if the Stone Guards move against him directly.
source_quote: I have been tracking a particular Duergar named Droki. He lives in the West Cleft District, where the Derro live.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum notices that the fire comes from a device the duergars are holding, a tube connected to a bottle on their back with a small flame outside the tube.
source_quote: Grygum notices that the fire comes from a device they are holding. It is a tube that connects to a bottle on their back. At the front of the tube, a small flame sits outside the tube.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realizes that the flame is produced from some kind of magic concoction lit by the tiny flame when the duergar operator pulls a lever.
source_quote: He realizes that the flame is produced from some kind of magic concoction lit by the tiny flame when the duergar operator pulls a lever.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thinks, 'Well, I guess Daz chose to weaken his spell purposely.'
source_quote: Grygum looks at Daz, and then looks at the giant, and thinks, 'Well, I guess Daz chose to weaken his spell purposely.'

subject: meeting with stone guards
fact: Errde invites them to her office for a friendly conversation in the Overlake Hold.
source_quote: I must ask that you come to my office so we can talk.

subject: offer expiration
fact: Gartokkar's offer expires tomorrow.
source_quote: The offer expires tomorrow.

subject: offer expiration by Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar’s offer of safe passage expires tomorrow, creating a time-sensitive decision point for Zalthir and the party.
source_quote: The offer expires tomorrow. And if you don’t accept the offer, I cannot promise we will be so friendly when we meet next.

subject: Red Dragon’s periodic replacement
fact: The Keepers of the Flame must regularly kill and replace the Red Dragon that powers the city’s furnaces, due to the dragon’s growing power and resentment of subordination. Dragon eggs are purchasable and hatchable, enabling this cycle.
source_quote: So the Keepers must kill and replace the dragon with a new one.

subject: shrinkage of enlarged Duergar
fact: After the stone giant’s death, the enlarged Duergar shrink back to their standard size, indicating a magical or temporary transformation tied to the battle’s conclusion.
source_quote: Grygum looks up, and the enlarged Duergars have shrunk to their standard size.

subject: shrinking of the Duergar
fact: After the death of the stone giant, the Duergar who used the flame device shrank to their standard size, suggesting their enlarged forms were magically sustained during the confrontation and were temporary. This shift was observed by Grygum and marked the end of the immediate threat.
source_quote: Grygum looks up, and the enlarged Duergars have shrunk to their standard size.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin notices that there seems to be something odd about Errde.
source_quote: Thorin pauses, 'Look, we want to know if this is for the Stone Guards or the City?' She pauses, and Thorin notices that there seems to be something odd about her

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wonders where exactly they will run to because it’s not clear how they can beat the entire stone guard.
source_quote: Thorin grabs his sword and wonders where exactly they will run to because it’s not clear how they can beat the entire stone guard

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir notices the scars on Gartokkar’s ears, four notches that don’t look self-inflicted.
source_quote: Zalthir immediately notices the scars on his ears, four notches that don’t look self-inflicted.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thinks, 'And that, too.'
source_quote: Zalthir thinks, 'And that, too.'

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thinks, 'I gotta get me some of that ability.'
source_quote: I gotta get me some of that ability," he thinks.

subject: Clan Lairds
fact: The Clan Lairds are suspected of involvement in the corruption at the Deepking’s court, with Droki possibly tied to their clandestine operations.
source_quote: He is linked to the Council of Savants and maybe even elements of the Clan Lairds.

subject: Council of Savants
fact: The Council of Savants is implicated in the corruption at the Deepking’s court, with Droki linked to its activities and possibly complicit in undermining its rules.
source_quote: He is linked to the Council of Savants and maybe even elements of the Clan Lairds.

subject: Crown
fact: The Crown is a faction in conflict with the Keepers of the Flame; its nature and goals are unknown, but it is implied to be a rival power structure within Gracklstugh.
source_quote: You must have met the Keepers of the Flame? They are in a pickle, what with the Gray Ghosts and the Crown.

subject: Deepking’s Court
fact: The Deepking’s court is suffering from systemic corruption: laws have become arbitrary, market rules are ignored, and chaos has replaced order; the court is suspected of being manipulated by hidden forces.
source_quote: The laws are more arbitrary... It’s as if he is detached from reality... Things were not proceeding according to the rules of the market... Then it proceeds to grift, then chaos, and then destruction.

subject: Duergar Patrol
fact: The Duergar patrol operates under the authority of the Deepking and is responsible for monitoring and suppressing anti-social, non-profitable madness among giants. They use magical flame devices to subdue or kill rogue stone giants. They are suspicious of non-Duergar authority, resentful of stone giants’ privileges, and maintain strict control over who enters or exits their city. They reported a recent surge in such incidents and acknowledged no known cause.
source_quote: “We have noticed that there have been significantly more incidents of this kind of behavior. As a result, the work of the militias has increased.”

subject: Duergar Regime
fact: The Duergar regime is characterized by brutal efficiency, arbitrary laws under the Deepking, and a complete absence of art or ceremony in governance. It is in decline, as its leaders are detached from reality and its institutions are increasingly unstable.
source_quote: Now, they don’t. It’s as if he is detached from reality.

subject: Gray Ghosts
fact: The Gray Ghosts are a faction in conflict with the Keepers of the Flame, though their motives and structure remain unclear; they are mentioned as a threat by the Halfling.
source_quote: You must have met the Keepers of the Flame? They are in a pickle, what with the Gray Ghosts and the Crown.

subject: Gray Ghosts
fact: The Gray Ghosts are a hostile faction opposing the Keepers of the Flame, likely a shadowy group of insurgents or assassins. They are in conflict with the Crown and are a threat to the stability of the Duergar regime.
source_quote: They are in a pickle, what with the Gray Ghosts and the Crown.

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are a powerful Duergar organization that controls the Red Dragon, providing it with a horde and pampering it to ensure its cooperation in maintaining the city’s furnaces. They are in a precarious position, as the dragon grows more powerful and resentful, and they must periodically kill and replace it. They are also threatened by the Gray Ghosts and the Crown.
source_quote: The keepers of the flame give him a horde, and they pamper him. The problem... is that Red Dragons dislike playing second fiddle. And so, at some point, the Dragon discovers it’s not in charge. Then, the Keepers of the Flame have to kill the dragon.

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are a prestigious faction within Gracklstugh, responsible for tending Themberchaud — a fire dragon that burns stone-hot to fuel the city’s furnaces. They are among the Deepking’s most prized advisors. They use a magical flame device to control the dragon’s output and operate under the authority of the Custodian of the Flame. They value utility and efficiency, and they have the power to grant safe passage and immunity from imprisonment.
source_quote: “I am the Custodian of the Flame, the chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who tend to Themberchaud’s needs.”

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame maintain Themberchaud, a red dragon used to heat Gracklstugh’s furnaces; they periodically kill and replace the dragon due to its growing power and resentment, and they are embroiled in conflict with the Gray Ghosts and the Crown.
source_quote: We use a fire dragon that burns stone hot... The problem... is that Red Dragons dislike playing second fiddle... the Keepers of the Flame have to kill the dragon... You must have met the Keepers of the Flame? They are in a pickle, what with the Gray Ghosts and the Crown.

subject: Stone Guards
fact: The Stone Guards are a faction of stone giants serving as enforcers or gatekeepers in Gracklstugh, loyal to their own kind and under the command of stone giants like Dorhun. They are distinct from Duergar authority and were ordered to grant Thorin passage despite Duergar disapproval, indicating their autonomy and higher status among the city’s non-Duergar powers.
source_quote: Turning to the Duergar with the stone weapons, he says, “Stone Guards, you are to let them through.”

subject: Stone Guards
fact: The Stone Guards are the official law enforcement of the city, loyal to the Duergar regime and operating from the Overlake Hold. They are pragmatic, austere, and prefer covert operations to avoid open conflict, especially with the Derro.
source_quote: I am Errde Blackskull, captain of the Stone Guards on the lake, and I must ask that you come to my office so we can talk.

subject: Stone Guards
fact: The Stone Guards, led by Errde Blackskull, are tasked with maintaining order in Gracklstugh; they are allied with Stone Giants and are investigating corruption linked to Droki, the Council of Savants, and Clan Lairds.
source_quote: I am Errde Blackskull, captain of the Stone Guards... We need someone who isn’t us to find him... Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption... I can tell them that they are not here.

subject: The Crown
fact: The Crown is a rival power to the Keepers of the Flame, possibly a royalist or centralized authority seeking to reclaim control over the Duergar city. It is in open conflict with both the Keepers and the Gray Ghosts.
source_quote: They are in a pickle, what with the Gray Ghosts and the Crown.

subject: Blade Bazaar
fact: Daz and his group arrive at the Blade Bazaar before going to the Darklake Brewery.
source_quote: from just outside the Blade Bazaar, Daz and his odd collection of travelers arrive at the Darklake Brewery.

subject: Cairngorm Cavern
fact: Cairngorm Cavern is a location in Gracklstugh, referenced by Dorhun as a place Thorin must visit before leaving the city. It is implied to be a site of significance to stone giant lore, possibly tied to the legacy of Stonespeaker Hgraam and the deeper history of the city’s giants.
source_quote: “I ask you to visit me at Cairngorm Cavern before you leave the city.”

subject: Cairngorm Cavern
fact: Cairngorm Cavern is the requested meeting place for Thorin and Dorhun, suggesting it holds significance for Stone Giant history or secrets related to Stonespeaker Hgraam.
source_quote: I ask you to visit me at Cairngorm Cavern before you leave the city.

subject: Cairngorm Cavern
fact: Dorhun invites Thorin to visit him at Cairngorm Cavern before leaving the city.
source_quote: I ask you to visit me at Cairngorm Cavern before you leave the city.

subject: Darklake Brewery
fact: Daz and his group arrive at the Darklake Brewery.
source_quote: Daz and his odd collection of travelers arrive at the Darklake Brewery.

subject: Darklake Brewery
fact: The Darklake Brewery is a closed establishment, accessible only to Duergar. It is a place of hushed conversations and covert information exchange, located just outside the Blade Bazaar. It is the site of key encounters with the halfling, Drow, and the Stone Guards.
source_quote: The Brewery is closed to non-Duergar, and Daz is disappointed until Grygum, who sneaks a quick peek, says that inside is a pretty dour place where people talk only in hushed whispers.

subject: Darklake Brewery
fact: The Darklake Brewery is a closed, hushed establishment outside the Blade Bazaar where the Halfling and Drow provide key intelligence on Gracklstugh’s factions and corruption.
source_quote: The Brewery is closed to non-Duergar... inside is a pretty dour place where people talk only in hushed whispers.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is a subterranean city ruled by the Deepking, where Duergar hold administrative power but stone giants retain ceremonial and military authority. The city relies on the Keepers of the Flame and their fire dragon, Themberchaud, to fuel its furnaces. It has prisons, militias, and a complex hierarchy where non-Duergar individuals require special permission to move freely. The city is marked by tension between Duergar control and stone giant autonomy.
source_quote: “Your skill set would be of great value to the city of Gracklstugh.”

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: The Duergar, unconvinced by Thorin’s entreaties, kill the giant.
source_quote: The Duergar, unconvinced by Thorin’s entreaties, kill the giant.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: The enlarged Duergars have shrunk to their standard size.
source_quote: Grygum looks up, and the enlarged Duergars have shrunk to their standard size.

subject: Overlake Hold
fact: Overlake Hold is the Stone Guards’ austere, stone-built guard house where Errde Blackskull offers Thorin’s party a bribe and protection in exchange for uncovering corruption.
source_quote: They are in the Overlake Hold, the local guard house... The chairs and table are made of stone. There is no color—the light is grey.

subject: Overlake Hold
fact: The Overlake Hold is the austere guardhouse and administrative center of the Stone Guards. Made entirely of grey stone, it reflects the cold, brutal efficiency of Duergar governance. It is where Errde Blackskull conducts official business and recruits covert agents.
source_quote: A few minutes later, they are in the Overlake Hold, the local guard house. Errde brings them to a sitting room. Like everything in this town, it is austere. The chairs and table are made of stone. There is no color—the light is grey.

subject: Overlake Hold
fact: The meeting takes place in the Overlake Hold, the local guard house.
source_quote: they are in the Overlake Hold, the local guard house.

subject: the city
fact: The city is the primary domain of the corruption, with the Deepking’s court at its heart, and Errde asserts her role as its protector against internal decay.
source_quote: There is something very wrong going on in my city. Some kind of corruption eats at the heart of the Deepking’s court.

subject: West Cleft District
fact: Droki lives in the West Cleft District, where the Derro live.
source_quote: Droki. He lives in the West Cleft District, where the Derro live.

subject: West Cleft District
fact: The West Cleft District is a Derro-inhabited area where the suspect Duergar, Droki, resides; it is considered too volatile for direct Stone Guard intervention.
source_quote: He lives in the West Cleft District, where the Derro live. If we were to go there in force, it would provoke a violent reaction.

subject: West Cleft District
fact: The West Cleft District is a dangerous neighborhood inhabited by the Derro. It is the suspected hideout of the rogue Duergar Droki and is considered too volatile for direct military incursion by the Stone Guards.
source_quote: He lives in the West Cleft District, where the Derro live.

subject: drow and halfling pair
fact: A Drow and a Halfling are drinking beer outside the Darklake Brewery.
source_quote: Just outside is a Drow and Halfing, and they are drinking beer.

subject: duergar attendants

source_quote: I am Gartokkar Xundorn, and these are my Duergar. Just then, a few other Duergar approaches to see what is happening.

subject: duergar patrol size
fact: Gartokkar is accompanied by his Duergar, and other Duergar approach to see what is happening.
source_quote: I am Gartokkar Xundorn, and these are my Duergar. Just then, a few other Duergar approaches to see what is happening.

source_quote: flanked by Duergar, armed with curious stone weapons. ...Stone Guards, you are to let them through.

subject: stone guards
fact: Dorhun is flanked by Duergar armed with curious stone weapons, referred to as Stone Guards.
source_quote: The Stone Giant stares at Thorin... flanked by Duergar, armed with curious stone weapons. ...Stone Guards, you are to let them through.

subject: stone guards patrol
fact: A group of Duergar with curious stone weapons, identified as Stone Guards, approach Thorin.
source_quote: Thorin downs his Darklake Brewery Stout... sees a group of Duergar with curious stone weapons approaching.

subject: two-headed stone giant
fact: The two-headed stone giant was subdued by Thorin but killed by Duergar using a magical flame device; it stood despite multiple attacks and magical bolts.
source_quote: The giant stands. The Duergar, unconvinced by Thorin’s entreaties, kill the giant.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz asks while holding down a snigger, 'So he’s a lighter?'
source_quote: Zalthir hears Daz ask while holding down a snigger, “So he’s a lighter?”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz cast magic that deliberately weakened the stone giant’s defenses, as observed by Grygum. He expressed amusement at Gartokkar’s description of the fire dragon as a ‘lighter,’ suppressing a snigger. He was intrigued by the mechanics of the dragon-fueled furnaces and the role of the Keepers of the Flame in Gracklstugh.
source_quote: Daz ask while holding down a snigger, “So he’s a lighter?”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz investigates the dragon-lighter system, questions the Halfling about factions and Deepking’s madness, recognizes the city’s corruption as rule-breaking behavior, and negotiates with Errde Blackskull for payment and freedom guarantees.
source_quote: How does a dragon end up turning into a lighter?" ... "In this authoritarian, strict-as-rules city, what we saw is corruption." ... "Of course, but we would need remuneration for all of that plus our time.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a traveler who seeks to understand the power dynamics of the Underdark, particularly regarding the Keepers of the Flame, the Red Dragon, and the Duergar regime. He is cautious about aligning with factions and values information over commitment.
source_quote: Daz wonders if they should interview the various factions to find out which one they should join or whether they should join any of them.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognizes corruption through the lens of the Blade Bazaar, having witnessed and replicated its behaviors — grift, chaos, and rule-breaking — and identifies systemic corruption in authoritarian structures.
source_quote: Yes, there was much of that going on.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz wonders why a red dragon would serve as a lighter, given that red dragons are not known for willingness to serve.
source_quote: How does a dragon end up turning into a lighter? What’s in it for him? Red dragons are not exactly known for their willingness to serve. They want to build a hoard or something. A dragon that flies around lighting fires is odd.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz wonders, 'How does a dragon end up turning into a lighter? What’s in it for him? Red dragons are not exactly known for their willingness to serve. They want to build a hoard or something. A dragon that flies around lighting fires is odd.'
source_quote: The story of this dragon intrigues Daz. “How does a dragon end up turning into a lighter? What’s in it for him? Red dragons are not exactly known for their willingness to serve. They want to build a hoard or something. A dragon that flies around lighting fires is odd.”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz’s hands emit a few bolts of magic.
source_quote: A few bolts of magic streak from Daz’s hands.

subject: Daz
fact: The story of the dragon intrigues Daz.
source_quote: The story of this dragon intrigues Daz.

subject: Dorhun
fact: Dorhun is a stone giant and former apprentice to Stonespeaker Hgraam. He confirmed Thorin’s account of trying to subdue Hgraam, explained that stone giants have qualified immunity if rampaging, and invited Thorin to visit Cairngorm Cavern before leaving the city. He introduced Rihuud as his companion and commanded Stone Guards to grant Thorin passage, despite the Duergar’s visible resentment.
source_quote: “I am Dorhun, and this is Rihuud. We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam. Did you kill him?”

subject: Dorhun
fact: Dorhun, a Stone Giant and former apprentice of Stonespeaker Hgraam, confirms Thorin’s account of the giant’s death and requests a meeting at Cairngorm Cavern, suggesting hidden knowledge or ritual significance.
source_quote: I am Dorhun... We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam. Did you kill him?

subject: Droki
fact: Droki is a Duergar suspected of corruption, residing in the West Cleft District among the Derro; he is linked to the Council of Savants and Clan Lairds, but his identity and actions are unconfirmed.
source_quote: I have been tracking a particular Duergar named Droki... Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption.

subject: Droki
fact: Droki is the central figure in the corruption at the Deepking’s court, linked to the Council of Savants and possibly elements of the Clan Lairds. His discovery is essential to proving the conspiracy.
source_quote: Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption.

subject: Drow
fact: The Drow is from Menzoberranzan and views Duergar violence as crude and artless compared to the refined politicking of his homeland. He is disgusted by the lack of style in Duergar conflict and contrasts their brutality with the elegance of drow intrigue.
source_quote: The backstabbing and politicking are nothing compared to the Duergar. I mean, we will do it with style and finesse. Here, it’s just slaughter. No torture, no speeches, no art, and I mean no style.

subject: Drow
fact: The Drow says, 'Look, friend, I am from Menzoberranzan. The backstabbing and politicking are nothing compared to the Duergar. I mean, we will do it with style and finesse. Here, it’s just slaughter. No torture, no speeches, no art, and I mean no style. It was just a brutal struggle. They just engage in violence for violence’s sake. It’s disgraceful if you ask me.'
source_quote: At this point, the Drow sitting next to the Halfling splutters, “Look, friend, I am from Menzoberranzan. The backstabbing and politicking are nothing compared to the Duergar. I mean, we will do it with style and finesse. Here, it’s just slaughter. No torture, no speeches, no art, and I mean no style. It was just a brutal struggle. They just engage in violence for violence’s sake. It’s disgraceful if you ask me.”

subject: Drow at Darklake Brewery
fact: The Drow from Menzoberranzan criticizes Duergar culture as brutish and styleless, contrasting it with Drow politicking, and implies deeper cultural tensions in the Underdark.
source_quote: The backstabbing and politicking are nothing compared to the Duergar... It’s just slaughter. No torture, no speeches, no art... It’s disgraceful.

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar gives the Stone Giant the briefest of scowls, showing how much they don’t want to give this non-Duergar permission to visit their city.
source_quote: The dwarf watches how the Duergar gives the Stone Giant the briefest of scowls, showing how much they don’t want to give this non-Duergar permission to visit their city.

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar says, 'And we know of no underlying cause. Although a clan leader may have information they have chosen not to share with us.'
source_quote: There is a pause, “And we know of no underlying cause. Although a clan leader may have information they have chosen not to share with us.”

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar turns to the others on his patrol, briefly discusses, and says, 'We have noticed that there have been significantly more incidents of this kind of behavior. As a result, the work of the militias has increased.'
source_quote: The Duergar turns to the others on his patrol, briefly discusses, and says, “We have noticed that there have been significantly more incidents of this kind of behavior. As a result, the work of the militias has increased.”

subject: Errde
fact: Errde is the guardian of the city against corruption, linked to the Council of Savants and possibly the Clan Lairds, and holds the key to uncovering the conspiracy centered on Droki. She can guarantee freedom and safe passage in exchange for Droki and proof of corruption.
source_quote: It is my job to protect the city from corruption. So yes, it is for the city.

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull is the captain of the Stone Guards on the lake, commanding authority through stern presence. She seeks covert assistance to locate the rogue Duergar Droki without provoking war with the Derro, and she navigates diplomacy with a mix of threat and charm.
source_quote: I have been tracking a particular Duergar named Droki. He lives in the West Cleft District, where the Derro live. If we were to go there in force, it would provoke a violent reaction. So we need someone who isn’t us to find him.

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull says, 'And I can offer one more thing. If a particular group of Drow were to come looking for some escaped slaves, I could tell them that they are not here. As you think about which group to work with, remember I am the one that can guarantee your freedom.'
source_quote: She then smiles very evilly, “And I can offer one more thing.” ... “If a particular group of Drow were to come looking for some escaped slaves, I could tell them that they are not here. As you think about which group to work with, remember I am the one that can guarantee your freedom.”

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull says, 'As a reward, I offer you 175 gold pieces of equipment from our armory. When you bring me Droki and the proof I need, then I will give you 175 more.'
source_quote: “As a reward, I offer you 175 gold pieces of equipment from our armory. When you bring me Droki and the proof I need, then I will give you 175 more.”

fact: Errde Blackskull says, 'I have been tracking a particular Duergar named Droki. He lives in the West Cleft District, where the Derro live. If we were to go there in force, it would provoke a violent reaction. So we need someone who isn’t us to find him.'
source_quote: “I have been tracking a particular Duergar named Droki. He lives in the West Cleft District, where the Derro live. If we were to go there in force, it would provoke a violent reaction. So we need someone who isn’t us to find him.”

And when that happens, I swear you will get free and safe passage out of the city.”

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull says, 'Things were not proceeding according to the rules of the market, of the bazaar. It starts with not obeying the rules. Then it proceeds to grift, then chaos, and then destruction.'
source_quote: Errde smiles, “Things were not proceeding according to the rules of the market, of the bazaar. It starts with not obeying the rules. Then it proceeds to grift, then chaos, and then destruction.”

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull, captain of the Stone Guards, manipulates Thorin’s party into investigating corruption, offers payment and protection, and implies authority over Drow slave claims; her motives are ambiguous.
source_quote: I can tell them that they are not here... I swear you will get free and safe passage out of the city.

subject: Gartokkar's status
fact: Gartokkar is the chief of the Keepers of the Flame and one of the Deepking’s most prized advisors.
source_quote: We are the most prized of the Deepking’s advisors.

subject: Gartokkar's title
fact: Gartokkar is the Custodian of the Flame and chief of the Keepers of the Flame.
source_quote: I am the Custodian of the Flame, the chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who tend to Themberchaud’s needs.

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn is the Custodian of the Flame and chief of the Keepers of the Flame, responsible for tending Themberchaud — a fire dragon that burns stone-hot to fuel Gracklstugh’s furnaces. He is literal-minded, misunderstood sarcasm, laughed at a joke for the first time in long memory, and offered Zalthir safe passage through the city in exchange for a service. He warned that the offer expires tomorrow and that future interactions may be hostile if declined.
source_quote: “Your skill set would be of great value to the city of Gracklstugh. If you were to come to the Keepers of the Flame headquarters and do me a service, I could give you safe passage through the city.”

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn says, 'I am the Custodian of the Flame, the chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who tend to Themberchaud’s needs.'
source_quote: “I am the Custodian of the Flame, the chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who tend to Themberchaud’s needs.”

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn says, 'The furnaces of Gracklstugh must be kept hot, and instead of using a large amount of kindling, we use a fire dragon that burns stone hot that then is used to keep the furnaces running.'
source_quote: “The furnaces of Gracklstugh must be kept hot, and instead of using a large amount of kindling, we use a fire dragon that burns stone hot that then is used to keep the furnaces running.”

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn says, 'The offer expires tomorrow. And if you don’t accept the offer, I cannot promise we will be so friendly when we meet next.'
source_quote: There is a moment of hesitation, “The offer expires tomorrow. And if you don’t accept the offer, I cannot promise we will be so friendly when we meet next.”

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn says, 'Yes. The Keepers of the Flame tend to the dragon’s needs. And we are the most prized of the Deepking’s advisors. We need someone like you.'
source_quote: Gartokkar is a Duergar, and he is literal and misses the sarcasm, “Yes. The Keepers of the Flame tend to the dragon’s needs. And we are the most prized of the Deepking’s advisors. We need someone like you.”

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn says, 'Your skill set would be of great value to the city of Gracklstugh. If you were to come to the Keepers of the Flame headquarters and do me a service, I could give you safe passage through the city. And as long as you did nothing that the Deepking would disapprove of and would not require me to do too much, I could keep you out of the prisons.'

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn, Custodian of the Flame and chief of the Keepers of the Flame, operates the dragon-lighter system for Gracklstugh’s furnaces and recruits outsiders; he laughs at jokes and makes conditional offers of protection.
source_quote: I am the Custodian of the Flame... We use a fire dragon that burns stone hot... We are the most prized of the Deepking’s advisors... We need someone like you.

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn, Custodian of the Flame, is literal, values humor, and recruits outsiders to serve the Keepers of the Flame; he is a high-ranking advisor to the Deepking.
source_quote: I am the Custodian of the Flame... We are the most prized of the Deepking’s advisors.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum hears from within the darkness the sound of Zalthir’s fists hitting the giant and the blade of Thorin, but still, the giant stands.
source_quote: Grygum hears from within the darkness the sound of Zalthir’’s fists hitting the giant and the blade of Thorin, but still, the giant stands.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is an orc who sneaks peeks to gather intelligence, speaks with pragmatic humor, and is perceived as non-threatening despite his appearance. He is trusted by Daz as a companion in navigating dangerous social terrain.
source_quote: Grygum, who sneaks a quick peek, says that inside is a pretty dour place where people talk only in hushed whispers.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum jokes, 'We do have some kindling here.'
source_quote: Zalthir hears Grygum’s joke, “We do have some kindling here.”

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum notices that the fire comes from a device the Duergar are holding, a tube that connects to a bottle on their back, with a small flame sitting outside the tube, produced by a magic concoction lit by a tiny flame when the Duergar operator pulls a lever.
source_quote: Grygum notices that the fire comes from a device they are holding. It is a tube that connects to a bottle on their back. At the front of the tube, a small flame sits outside the tube. He realizes that the flame is produced from some kind of magic concoction lit by the tiny flame when the duergar operator pulls a lever.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum observes the battle, interprets Daz’s magic as deliberately weakened, hears Zalthir’s attacks, and rushes in to strike the giant with his mace; he later witnesses Thorin praying and the Duergar shrinking.
source_quote: Grygum looks at Daz, and then looks at the giant, and thinks, 'Well, I guess Daz chose to weaken his spell purposely.' ... Grygum rushes in to strike with his mace. ... Grygum watches as a distraught Thorin whispers prayers for the dead. ... Grygum looks up, and the enlarged Duergars have shrunk to their standard size.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum rushes in to strike with his mace.
source_quote: So Grygum rushes in to strike with his mace.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thinks, 'Well, I guess Daz chose to weaken his spell purposely.'
source_quote: Grygum looks at Daz, and then looks at the giant, and thinks, “Well, I guess Daz chose to weaken his spell purposely.”

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum watches as a distraught Thorin whispers prayers for the dead.
source_quote: Grygum watches as a distraught Thorin whispers prayers for the dead.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum witnessed the death of a two-headed stone giant at the hands of Duergar using a magical flame device, observed Thorin’s attempt to subdue it, noted Daz’s deliberate weakening of his spells, and heard Zalthir’s fists and Thorin’s blade striking the giant — ultimately rushing in to strike with his mace. He watched Thorin mourn the giant and saw the Duergar shrink to standard size after the giant’s death.
source_quote: Grygum looks at Daz, and then looks at the giant, and thinks, “Well, I guess Daz chose to weaken his spell purposely.”

subject: Guard
fact: The guard sensing that asks, 'Someone who does not follow orders and engages in anti-social behavior, but does it in a way that will bring them no profit and certain doom?'
source_quote: The guard sensing that asks, “Someone who does not follow orders and engages in anti-social behavior, but does it in a way that will bring them no profit and certain doom?”

subject: Halfling
fact: The halfling is an outsider in the Underdark who survives by appearing harmless, avoiding political entanglements, and sharing information with those not 'in the game.' He is well-informed about factional conflicts, the Deepking’s madness, and the Keepers of the Flame’s predicament.
source_quote: I’m an outsider. And what do I know? Not very much. And as long as I stay an outsider, no one considers me a threat. And I can share what I know with those not in the game. And you are not part of the game, nor am I.

subject: Halfling
fact: The halfling says, 'It all began with the Deepking’s madness.'
source_quote: “It all began with the Deepking’s madness.”

subject: Halfling
fact: The halfling says, 'I’m an outsider. And what do I know? Not very much. And as long as I stay an outsider, no one considers me a threat. And I can share what I know with those not in the game. And you are not part of the game, nor am I.'
source_quote: “I’m an outsider. And what do I know? Not very much. And as long as I stay an outsider, no one considers me a threat. And I can share what I know with those not in the game. And you are not part of the game, nor am I.”

subject: Halfling
fact: The halfling says, 'Now, they don’t. It’s as if he is detached from reality.'
source_quote: Now, they don’t. It’s as if he is detached from reality.

subject: Halfling
fact: The halfling says, 'The red dragon keeps the stones hot enough for the furnaces to burn. Are you wondering about its horde? The keepers of the flame give him a horde, and they pamper him. The problem, and you’re right to wonder, is that Red Dragons dislike playing second fiddle. And so, at some point, the Dragon discovers it’s not in charge. Then, the Keepers of the Flame have to kill the dragon. There is also the problem of the dragon becoming more powerful over time. So the Keepers must kill and replace the dragon with a new one.'
source_quote: “The red dragon keeps the stones hot enough for the furnaces to burn. Are you wondering about its horde? The keepers of the flame give him a horde, and they pamper him. The problem, and you’re right to wonder, is that Red Dragons dislike playing second fiddle. And so, at some point, the Dragon discovers it’s not in charge. Then, the Keepers of the Flame have to kill the dragon. There is also the problem of the dragon becoming more powerful over time. So the Keepers must kill and replace the dragon with a new one.”

subject: Halfling
fact: The halfling says, 'What is that expression? It's -- Not relevant to the game.'
source_quote: He pauses, searching for a phrase, “What is that expression? It's -- Not relevant to the game.”

subject: Halfling
fact: The halfling says, 'You must have met the Keepers of the Flame? They are in a pickle, what with the Gray Ghosts and the Crown.'
source_quote: “You must have met the Keepers of the Flame? They are in a pickle, what with the Gray Ghosts and the Crown.”

subject: Halfling at Darklake Brewery
fact: The Halfling is an outsider who avoids faction involvement, provides key intelligence on Deepking’s madness and faction conflicts, and understands the danger of being perceived as a player.
source_quote: I’m an outsider... As long as I stay an outsider, no one considers me a threat... Not relevant to the game.

subject: Rihuud
fact: Rihuud is Dorhun’s companion, a Stone Giant and former apprentice of Stonespeaker Hgraam; his role is passive but confirms the legitimacy of Dorhun’s request.
source_quote: I am Dorhun, and this is Rihuud. We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam.

subject: Rihuud
fact: Rihuud is a stone giant and companion of Dorhun, also an apprentice of Stonespeaker Hgraam. He accompanied Dorhun when he met Thorin and was present when Dorhun granted passage through the city. He did not speak but was part of the authoritative presence that commanded the Stone Guards.
source_quote: “I am Dorhun, and this is Rihuud. We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam.”

subject: Stone Giant
fact: The Stone Giant says to the Duergar with the stone weapons, 'Stone Guards, you are to let them through.'
source_quote: Turning to the Duergar with the stone weapons, he says, “Stone Guards, you are to let them through.”

subject: Stone Giant
fact: The Stone Giant says, 'I am Dorhun, and this is Rihuud. We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam. Did you kill him?'
source_quote: The Stone Giant doesn’t smile, “No. But then again, I don’t know many. Who are you?” ... Then he says, “I am Dorhun, and this is Rihuud. We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam. Did you kill him?”

subject: Stone Giant
fact: The Stone Giant says, 'I ask you to visit me at Cairngorm Cavern before you leave the city.'
source_quote: Then he says, “I ask you to visit me at Cairngorm Cavern before you leave the city.”

subject: Stone Giant
fact: The Stone Giant says, 'We have qualified immunity if a Stone Giant is rampaging through our city.'
source_quote: “We have qualified immunity if a Stone Giant is rampaging through our city,” one explains.

subject: Stone Giant
fact: The Stone Giant stares at Thorin, whose body and blade show that he fought and perhaps killed the two-headed giant.
source_quote: The Stone Giant stares at Thorin, whose body and blade show that he fought and perhaps killed the two-headed giant.

subject: Stonespeaker Hgraam
fact: Stonespeaker Hgraam was the mentor of Dorhun and Rihuud; his death is implied to be connected to the stone giant’s rampage and the city’s deeper mysteries.
source_quote: We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam. Did you kill him?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin attempted to subdue the two-headed stone giant, pleaded with the Duergar not to kill it, and later prayed for the dead. He inquired about unusual behavior among giants, used a precise definition of anti-social, non-profitable madness to communicate with the Duergar, and was directed by Dorhun — a stone giant apprentice of Stonespeaker Hgraam — to visit Cairngorm Cavern. He confirmed that he tried to subdue Hgraam, not kill him, and was granted safe passage by the Stone Guards.
source_quote: “Don’t kill him! There’s something wrong with this giant! Let’s try and subdue him,” shouts Thorin.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin attempts to subdue the stone giant, prays for the dead, questions Duergar about 'crazy' behavior, learns of increased incidents of anti-social giants, and is approached by Dorhun who requests a visit to Cairngorm Cavern; he later negotiates with Errde Blackskull and seeks clarity on whether he serves the city or the Stone Guards.
source_quote: Don’t kill him! There’s something wrong with this giant! Let’s try and subdue him," ... "Are there more crazy people about?" ... "I ask you to visit me at Cairngorm Cavern before you leave the city." ... "It’s just a friendly meeting. Not that kind of meeting!" ... "Are we helping you? Or the city?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a traveler who is tempted to join the Stone Guards but is wary of factional entanglements. He is influenced by the halfling’s warnings and struggles to distinguish between helping the guards and serving the city’s interests.
source_quote: Are we helping you? Or the city?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is seeking clarity on whether to align with the Stone Guards or the City, and is being manipulated by Errde’s promises of freedom and rewards in exchange for action against Droki.
source_quote: Look, we want to know if this is for the Stone Guards or the City?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is tempted to work for the Stone Guards, but the warnings of the halfling worry him.
source_quote: Thorin is tempted to work for the Stone Guards. After all, they are friends of the Stone giants, but the warnings of the Halfing worry him.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is unfamiliar with the patterns of behavior of the Duergar, and finds the madness of a stone giant unheard of.
source_quote: Although Thorin is unfamiliar with the patterns of behavior of the Duergar, the madness of a stone giant is unheard of.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin remembers that Stone Giants are not talkative and may take a long time before they initiate a conversation as they ponder all possible things.
source_quote: Thorin remembers that Stone Giants are not talkative and may take a long time before they initiate a conversation as they ponder all possible things.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin says, 'It’s just a friendly meeting. Not that kind of meeting!'
source_quote: Thorin grabs his sword and wonders where exactly they will run to because it’s not clear how they can beat the entire stone guard, but the effect Daz was hoping for is achieved. Errde is taken aback and smiles, “Of course not. It is a friendly conversation.” ... Thorin shouts, “It’s just a friendly meeting. Not that kind of meeting!”

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin shouts, 'Don’t kill him! There’s something wrong with this giant! Let’s try and subdue him.'
source_quote: “Don’t kill him! There’s something wrong with this giant! Let’s try and subdue him,” shouts Thorin.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin turns to one of the Duergar, 'Are there more crazy people about?'
source_quote: He turns to one of the Duergar, “Are there more crazy people about?”

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin whispers prayers for the dead after the duergars kill the giant.
source_quote: Grygum watches as a distraught Thorin whispers prayers for the dead.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is targeted by Gartokkar Xundorn, Custodian of the Flame, who offers him safe passage through Gracklstugh in exchange for service; the offer expires tomorrow and carries implied threats.
source_quote: I am the Custodian of the Flame... Your skill set would be of great value to the city of Gracklstugh... The offer expires tomorrow. And if you don’t accept the offer, I cannot promise we will be so friendly when we meet next.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is trying hard to protect himself from being burned alive, crushed by a giant, or arrested.
source_quote: Zalthir is trying hard to protect himself from being burned alive, crushed by a giant, or arrested.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thinks, 'I gotta get me some of that ability.'
source_quote: “I gotta get me some of that ability,” he thinks.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir was focused on survival against being burned, crushed, or arrested. He encountered Gartokkar Xundorn, Custodian of the Flame and chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who offered him safe passage through Gracklstugh in exchange for a service. Gartokkar revealed the city’s use of a fire dragon to fuel furnaces, misunderstood sarcasm about being a ‘lighter,’ and laughed at Grygum’s joke about kindling. Zalthir was warned the offer expires tomorrow and that future encounters may not be friendly.
source_quote: “I am the Custodian of the Flame, the chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who tend to Themberchaud’s needs.”

subject: Zalthir's observation
fact: Zalthir notices Gartokkar has four notches on his ears, which do not look self-inflicted.
source_quote: Zalthir immediately notices the scars on his ears, four notches that don’t look self-inflicted.

subject: 175 gold pieces of equipment
fact: Errde offers 175 gold pieces of equipment from the armory as a reward for initial cooperation, with another 175 gold pieces contingent on delivering Droki and proof of corruption.
source_quote: As a reward, I offer you 175 gold pieces of equipment from our armory. When you bring me Droki and the proof I need, then I will give you 175 more.

subject: Dragon eggs
fact: Dragon eggs are available for purchase and can be hatched, enabling the Keepers of the Flame to replace the Red Dragon when necessary. This knowledge informs Daz’s understanding of the cycle of control and violence in the city.
source_quote: Daz wonders... how Dragon eggs can be purchased and hatched.

subject: Flame Device
fact: The flame device is a magical apparatus used by Duergar to control and project fire, consisting of a tube connected to a bottle on the back, with a small external flame produced by a magic concoction lit when a lever is pulled. It was used to kill the two-headed stone giant and is a signature tool of the Duergar militias.
source_quote: It is a tube that connects to a bottle on their back. At the front of the tube, a small flame sits outside the tube. He realizes that the flame is produced from some kind of magic concoction lit by the tiny flame when the duergar operator pulls a lever.

subject: flame tube and bottle device
fact: A Duergar-held device consisting of a tube connected to a bottle on the back produces a persistent flame through magic; it is used to burn and kill the stone giant.
source_quote: It is a tube that connects to a bottle on their back. At the front of the tube, a small flame sits outside the tube. He realizes that the flame is produced from some kind of magic concoction lit by the tiny flame when the duergar operator pulls a lever.

subject: reward offer
fact: Errde offers 175 gold pieces of equipment from the armory as initial reward, with another 175 gold pieces upon success.
source_quote: I offer you 175 gold pieces of equipment from our armory. When you bring me Droki and the proof I need, then I will give you 175 more.

subject: reward structure
fact: Errde offers 175 gold pieces upfront and another 175 gold pieces upon successful delivery of Droki and proof.
source_quote: I offer you 175 gold pieces of equipment from our armory. When you bring me Droki and the proof I need, then I will give you 175 more.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a fire dragon kept by the Keepers of the Flame in Gracklstugh. It burns stone-hot and is used to fuel the city’s furnaces, replacing the need for large amounts of kindling. It is a living, controlled weapon of industrial power, and its care is the most prized duty in the Deepking’s service.
source_quote: “we use a fire dragon that burns stone hot that then is used to keep the furnaces running.”

subject: corruption inquiry
fact: Errde seeks proof of corruption linked to Droki, the Council of Savants, and Clan Lairds.
source_quote: Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption. He is linked to the Council of Savants and maybe even elements of the Clan Lairds.

subject: corruption of the Deepking’s court
fact: A hidden corruption is eating at the heart of the Deepking’s court, linked to Droki, the Council of Savants, and Clan Lairds; its nature and resolution remain unresolved.
source_quote: There is something very wrong going on in my city. Some kind of corruption eats at the heart of the Deepking’s court. Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption.

subject: Deepking’s madness
fact: The Deepking’s rule has become increasingly arbitrary and detached from reality, leading to the collapse of logical law in Gracklstugh. This madness is the root cause of current factional instability and the Keepers of the Flame’s desperation.
source_quote: It all began with the Deepking’s madness.

subject: Dorhun’s invitation to Cairngorm Cavern
fact: Dorhun invited Thorin to visit Cairngorm Cavern before leaving the city, implying that Hgraam’s legacy, the stone giants’ history, or a deeper secret lies there. This is an unresolved thread that may connect to the mystery of the giant madness, the Duergar’s control, or the origins of the fire dragon.
source_quote: “I ask you to visit me at Cairngorm Cavern before you leave the city.”

subject: Droki’s corruption
fact: Droki is linked to the Council of Savants and maybe even elements of the Clan Lairds, but the nature of this corruption is not yet proven.
source_quote: Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption. He is linked to the Council of Savants and maybe even elements of the Clan Lairds.

subject: Drow slave escape
fact: A group of escaped Drow slaves may be in the city; Errde Blackskull offers to deny their presence, implying the party may be harboring them or could be targeted by Menzoberranzan.
source_quote: If a particular group of Drow were to come looking for some escaped slaves, I could tell them that they are not here.

subject: escaped slaves
fact: A group of Drow may be searching for escaped slaves; Errde can deny their presence in the city, and her ability to provide this cover is a leverage point for Thorin’s freedom.
source_quote: If a particular group of Drow were to come looking for some escaped slaves, I could tell them that they are not here.

subject: Gartokkar’s offer to Zalthir
fact: Gartokkar offered Zalthir safe passage and protection in Gracklstugh in exchange for a service, with the offer expiring tomorrow. Failure to accept may result in hostile future encounters. The nature of the service is unspecified, creating a pending plot thread that could lead Zalthir into the heart of the Keepers of the Flame’s operations.
source_quote: “The offer expires tomorrow. And if you don’t accept the offer, I cannot promise we will be so friendly when we meet next.”

subject: identity and fate of Droki
fact: Droki, a Duergar living in the West Cleft District, is the central figure in the corruption investigation; his connection to the Council of Savants and Clan Lairds is unverified.
source_quote: I have been tracking a particular Duergar named Droki... Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption.

subject: mystery of the stone giant madness
fact: A surge of anti-social, non-profitable madness among stone giants has been reported by Duergar, with no known cause. This phenomenon has increased militia work and may be tied to a clan leader’s hidden knowledge. Thorin and Dorhun’s encounters suggest this is a systemic issue with deep roots in the city’s power structure.
source_quote: “We have noticed that there have been significantly more incidents of this kind of behavior... And we know of no underlying cause. Although a clan leader may have information they have chosen not to share with us.”

subject: Not relevant to the game
fact: The phrase 'Not relevant to the game' has emerged as a cryptic mantra among outsiders who avoid factional entanglements. It defines a survival philosophy in the Underdark, separating observers from participants.
source_quote: What is that expression? It's -- Not relevant to the game.

subject: origin of the dragon-lighter system
fact: The origin of the red dragon’s forced servitude as a flame source for Gracklstugh’s furnaces is unexplained, and the cycle of killing and replacing dragons raises ethical and strategic questions.
source_quote: The Keepers of the Flame give him a horde, and they pamper him... the Keepers must kill and replace the dragon with a new one.

subject: proof of corruption
fact: Errde claims Daz’s description of the Blade Bazaar’s behaviors constitutes proof of corruption, linking systemic lawlessness in commerce to political decay.
source_quote: You have found me proof!

subject: The Halfling’s outsider status
fact: The halfling refuses to become involved in the city’s factions because he wants to remain an outsider who watches, not participates.
source_quote: I like to watch. I would avoid such encounters and actions.

subject: The Red Dragon’s fate
fact: The Keepers of the Flame must kill and replace the red dragon over time because it becomes more powerful and resents its role, but the source of new dragons is unexplored.
source_quote: So the Keepers must kill and replace the dragon with a new one.

subject: Thorin’s allegiance
fact: Thorin is torn between aiding the Stone Guards, the city, or remaining neutral; his moral compass conflicts with the city’s authoritarian structure and hidden agendas.
source_quote: Are we helping you? Or the city?" ... "I am tempted to work for the Stone Guards... but the warnings of the Halfing worry him.

subject: Zalthir’s desire for power
fact: Zalthir wants to acquire the ability he saw used by Gartokkar, but his intention to do so is unspoken beyond his internal thought.
source_quote: I gotta get me some of that ability," he thinks.

subject: Zalthir’s recruitment
fact: Zalthir has been offered a role in the Keepers of the Flame, but the cost, timing, and consequences of acceptance remain unknown.
source_quote: Your skill set would be of great value... I could give you safe passage... I cannot promise we will be so friendly when we meet next.
